title: GB Home Flex Explorer
tagline: How much could a home save by using electricity when it's cheapest?
description: A live calculator that uses real Ofgem and Elexon data to show how much a British household could save by charging an electric car or a home battery when power is cheap, and how other European countries compare.
longDescription:
Electricity costs more at some times of day than at others. It is cheap overnight and when it's windy, and expensive around teatime when everyone is cooking and the heating is on. Most homes pay one flat price, so they never see this difference. A **flexible** home uses power when it is cheap instead, for example by charging an electric car overnight or filling a home battery and using it later.

This app answers a simple question: **how much money is that actually worth?**

### What it does

- **Uses real prices.** It downloads the current price cap from Ofgem and a full year of half-hourly wholesale prices from Elexon, the body that runs Britain's electricity market. Nothing is made up. If a source can't be reached, the app says so instead of guessing.
- **Compares bills side by side.** A typical home on a flat price, then on a price that changes through the day, then with a smart-charged electric car, then with a home battery as well.
- **Answers "is it worth buying?"** For a battery, it estimates how many years it takes for the savings to pay back the cost.
- **Compares Europe.** A scorecard shows how ready the Netherlands, Germany, France, Ireland and Spain are, with sources, and downloads as a one-page PDF.

### Why it's helpful

- **For households:** a clear answer, in pounds, to "should I switch tariff, set my car to charge overnight, or buy a battery?"
- **For energy companies and policy teams:** a quick, transparent way to see the value of flexible homes. Every number traces back to a public source.
- **For the grid:** when homes use less power at the busiest times, the system needs fewer expensive power stations on standby. That keeps costs down for everyone.

### Try it

Change the settings in the sidebar, such as how much your car drives or how big the battery is, and the results update straight away. Every assumption is listed in the **Sources & method** tab.

> The first load fetches live data and takes about 10 seconds. If the app has been asleep, press the wake-up button inside the frame.
